Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashutosh Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anil Kumar Chaudhary,Shashank Shekhar Rai
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant; learned A.G.A. for the State; learned counsel for informant and perused the record.

2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.306 of 2023, under Sections 342, 376, 504, 506 I.P.C.,
P.S.Muhammadabad Gohna, District Mau, during pendency of the trial.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
On perusal of record, it appears that instant F.I.R. is malicious prosecution and has been lodged only to harass the applicant.

It is next submitted that before lodging the F.I.R. victim moved an application on 21.03.2023 alleging that victim and Nikhil Nigam vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41873963/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: applicants were in love since last one year and victim often met with applicant at his house.
When applicant refused to marry with the victim then the instant F.I.R. has been lodged.
Counsel for the applicant has further submitted that on 13.10.2023 a missing report has been lodged by the mother of the applicant regarding victim's missing from her house.

As per medical examination report,
victim is aged about 18 years.
The applicant, earlier proposed the marriage with victim but victim was found missing from her parents house which is evident from the missing report dated 13.10.2023.
The medical report and other evidence collected are not supporting the prosecution case.
The applicant has no criminal antecedent.
Moreover, there is no prospect of trial of the present case being concluded in near future.

The applicant is languishing in jail since 27.11.2023 and in case,
he is enlarged on bail he will not misuse the liberty of bail and co-operate in trial.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer of the applicant.

5. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of offence, evidence, complicity of accused and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant, Nikhil Nigam, who is involved in the aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
7. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Order Date :- 15.2.2024
